feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications/platform leader: the scope, progression, and public-sector specialization come through clearly. It is well written overall, but it is slightly repetitive, overly dense in places, and could sharpen impact by reducing duplication and adding more outcome-focused metrics.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within one organization, culminating in director/consulting leadership roles; this supports credibility and seniority.  
- Strong domain positioning: digital platforms, governance, analytics, editorial systems, multimedia, and AI-enabled search are consistently presented.  
- Good use of scale indicators (10,000+ pages, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers), which adds substance and impact.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce redundancy across Core Competencies, Topline Skills, Technical + IT, and Recent Projects; several themes/tools repeat, making the CV feel longer than necessary.  
- Add more measurable outcomes beyond scope metrics—for example, engagement growth, efficiency gains, reduced publishing time, campaign performance, or adoption improvements.  
- Fix minor style/consistency issues: “organization wide” should be “organization-wide”; punctuation in lists is inconsistent (e.g., “social, and multimedia” vs. other lists); “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization is stylistically inconsistent unless intentional branding. No major spelling errors found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus. It would be sharper with one concrete scale indicator and slightly less overlap with the subtitle, core competencies, and recent experience bullets.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Add a measurable scope point to increase impact, e.g., “10,000+ page platforms,” “3.5M annual page views,” or “50+ publishers.”
- Tighten phrasing: change “building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind” to “leading digital platforms, governance, and content operations for.”
- Prioritize the most relevant strengths for target roles: web modernization, governance, analytics, and AI-enabled search/content experiences.
- Consider a cleaner rewrite: “Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience leading web modernization, governance, analytics, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Delivers scalable editorial systems, multimedia programs, and AI-enabled search and content experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with Core Competencies and Recent Projects; consider narrowing to “AI-enabled search and content experiences.”
- “Multimedia production” is repeated across the intro, competencies, and work history.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be more effective if tightened to emphasize distinctive capability areas rather than repeating broad phrases already used elsewhere.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use shorter, sharper competency labels: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, dashboards and reporting • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations
- Replace “Multi-channel communications operations” with a more specific phrase such as “Cross-channel content operations” or remove it if space is tight.
- Standardize style by avoiding mixed constructions like “systems,” “infrastructure,” “operations,” and “experiences” unless each adds clear meaning.
- Consider ordering by strongest/recentest value: web modernization, AI search, analytics, governance, automation, advocacy, multimedia.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “AI-enabled search,” and “analytics infrastructure” are already prominent in the header and Topline Skills.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” overlaps with both the header and multiple NACo roles.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshots that reinforce the CV’s themes, but the footer is text-dense and overlaps with work experience. Tightening phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Use stronger, more specific verbs and simplify phrasing: e.g., “Created an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content, and bill-level chat.”
- Where possible, add scale or outcome signals (audience, usage, campaign purpose, conference/event context) to make impact clearer.
- Standardize style and punctuation: use sentence case consistently, and spell out “10 x 20-foot” instead of “10×20-foot” for CV readability.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series closely repeat achievements already covered in recent NACo roles.
- “Built”/“developed” repeats across entries; vary verbs to avoid sounding formulaic.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the NACo role below and Recent Projects. Tighten it around consulting impact, platform outcomes, and what is new since returning as a consultant.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on digital strategy, Drupal platform enhancements, content operations, and enterprise web modernization for member-facing communications.”
- Replace generic verbs with outcome-oriented phrasing: “Designed/implemented,” “streamlined,” “launched,” “improved,” “advised leadership on.”
- Consolidate into 4 bullets, e.g.:
- Advise on digital strategy, governance, and cross-channel operating models across web, email, social, and multimedia.
- Designed Drupal campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits.
- Improved CMS workflows, front-end implementation, and troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Led an AI-enabled search initiative covering retrieval strategy, structured content design, and discovery UX.
- Add metrics if available: number of sites/pages, publishing time reduced, engagement lift, search success, toolkit downloads.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics” overlaps with Director of Digital Media.
- Microsite and AI search details duplicate Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level if those project blurbs remain.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground the biggest outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management points already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + leadership: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Combine the strongest platform metrics into one bullet: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make outcomes more explicit where possible: add team size, budget, % efficiency gains, reporting adoption, production cost savings, or engagement growth for email/social/video.
- Tighten weaker bullets: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio for advocacy, events, and recurring multimedia content” and “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery to strengthen reporting and decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Governance/publishing workflow language also appears in the current consultant role; differentiate this as organization-wide operational leadership.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry reads generic and overlaps with the more senior NACo roles. Tighten it around executional leadership, cross-team coordination, and any measurable channel growth or workflow improvements.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and ownership: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Combine related bullets and sharpen verbs: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more outcome-focused: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.” Add views, cadence, or engagement lift if available.
- Replace vague phrasing like “helped improve” with direct contribution and results: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role and footer project; distinguish this entry as scaling/operationalizing the program.
- Avoid repeating broad channel oversight already covered more strongly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should be tightened to emphasize senior strategic scope and avoid repeating wording already proven in recent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic phrases with sharper, higher-level language:  
  Enterprise digital strategy • Editorial governance & content operations • Cross-channel communications leadership • Public-sector advocacy communications • Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “messaging” for “communications” or “strategy” to sound more senior and less tactical.
- Keep terms aligned with recent experience: “content operations,” “editorial governance,” and “cross-channel” map better to 2022–Present work than “audience-focused content planning.”
- If space allows, make one item more distinctive, e.g. “Enterprise web and communications strategy” to connect directly to modernization leadership.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” repeat the header/Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” also overlaps with Core Competencies; “cross-channel communications leadership” is a cleaner variation.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. For a topline skills area, emphasize higher-value capabilities and recent strengths rather than enumerating every platform.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- Put Drupal first and keep WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages only if they are important for target roles; otherwise cut 1–2 lower-priority platforms.
- Replace “Airtable systems” with a more outcome-oriented phrase like “Airtable-based workflow systems” or “operational workflow systems.”
- If space allows, add one impact cue tied to recent work: “enterprise CMS modernization” or “large public-facing web properties.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search experiences” duplicates Core Competencies and recent project content; keep here only if shortened elsewhere.
- Most tools repeat the “Technical + IT” section; this topline item should stay selective, not exhaustive.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for the recent Director/Consultant work, but it reads as a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and “Technical + IT.” Make it more outcome-oriented and slightly more strategic.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Analytics, Reporting & Optimization**
- Replace with: **GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Looker Studio, Power BI and BigQuery • Analytics infrastructure and dashboard development • KPI framework design and leadership reporting • SEO, user behavior and performance analysis**
- Group tools first, then capabilities; this improves scanability and sounds more senior than a flat list.
- If you can support it elsewhere, consider adding one impact cue such as: **decision-ready reporting** or **cross-channel performance measurement**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially duplicates **Technical + IT → Data, Analytics & Optimization**; keep this version strategic and let Technical + IT hold the fuller tool inventory.
- “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” already appears in **Core Competencies**, so avoid repeating that exact phrase.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but it’s too generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities tied to studio buildout and event delivery leadership rather than basic production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from task list to capability/outcome language: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio operations • PTZ/multi-camera production systems • Virtual event execution”
- Consider replacing “Video production and editing” with “Broadcast-quality video production” to better match the Director-level studio achievement.
- If space allows, add scope/leadership nuance: “Livestream and hybrid event production” instead of separate “Livestreaming” and “Hybrid and virtual event production.”
- Keep tool-specific detail like PTZ, but only if this role targets multimedia/event operations; otherwise swap for “multi-camera production systems” for broader relevance.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies.
- Tool-level overlap with “Livestream studio workflows” in Technical + IT; avoid repeating the same phrasing.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” skills section. This item should either add nuance on level of use or be tightened to emphasize the most current, highest-value platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • SharePoint • WordPress • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add proficiency context: **Drupal (enterprise/public-sector web modernization) • SharePoint (intranets/collaboration) • WordPress • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Consider dropping **GitHub Pages** unless it reflects meaningful recent work; it feels lighter-weight than the rest.
- If you want stronger impact, rename to **CMS & Web Platforms** and align wording with recent experience in Drupal-led modernization.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely repeats the **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution** entry; consider consolidating or using one section for platform names and the other for broader capabilities.
- Drupal is already heavily evidenced in recent roles, so avoid overemphasizing it in multiple places without adding new context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical range, but this reads like a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. For a senior digital leader, emphasize implementation depth and modern tools rather than basic languages alone.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to show applied capability, e.g. “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Group by function for clarity: “Integrations & tagging: API integrations, Google Tag Manager”
- Keep the more distinctive tools that support recent work: “Serverless & deployment: Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- If true, upgrade with scope/outcome language elsewhere or inline: “used for CMS customization, campaign microsites, workflow automation, and analytics deployment”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills; consider shortening one version.
- “Google Tag Manager” may fit better under “Data, Analytics & Optimization” unless tagging implementation is a core differentiator.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow leadership. Since workflow automation already appears in Core Competencies and Topline Skills, this item should be tighter and more systems-oriented.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe by function, not just brand names: “Workflow automation & work management: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier; project/issue tracking: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp; collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams.”
- Put the strongest, most relevant tools first: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana.
- If accurate, add a light qualifier to show depth: “built workflow systems in Airtable and Power Automate” or “used to support cross-team publishing and campaign operations.”
- Consider dropping one or two lower-value/general tools (e.g., Slack, Teams) if space is tight; they don’t differentiate senior capability.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” is already stated in Core Competencies and Topline Skills; avoid repeating that exact phrase elsewhere without adding specificity.
- Airtable systems and workflow automation also appear under Web Platforms & Technical Execution, so this item should complement, not mirror, that section.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as generic software inventory rather than evidence of email/engagement capability. Since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles, this item should stay concise and tool-focused.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten formatting and standardize product names: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add one qualifier to show level of use without repeating work history, e.g. **enterprise email automation, newsletter operations, audience engagement**
- Consider ordering by strongest/recent relevance: put the platform most used in recent roles first

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding outcomes like newsletter reach or channel leadership here; those are already covered in the 2022–2024 and 2018–2022 NACo roles.
- “Engagement” overlaps with broader multi-channel communications language elsewhere, so keep this item specifically about email/marketing platforms.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills” and repeats analytics detail already proven in the recent Director role. Tighten it into a more differentiated technical stack entry and make the optimization angle clearer.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Analytics & Optimization Tools**
- Replace with: **GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Google Search Console • SEO analysis • Experimentation / A/B testing**
- Swap vague **Dashboarding** for actual platforms or capability language; dashboards are already implied by Looker Studio/Power BI.
- If space allows, order by strongest/recent tools first: **GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Clarity** to align with your 2022–2024 leadership work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates **Topline Skills → Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider trimming one or making Topline more strategic and this one purely tool-based.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the Director role, so avoid adding extra descriptive wording here unless it introduces new specificity.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful “first in-house digital team” context, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and, if possible, quantify scope or outputs.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize foundational impact: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and establish workflows spanning web, email, social media and multimedia production.”
- Tighten the second sentence around concrete contributions: “Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates, to expand the organization’s owned-media capacity.”
- Replace “high-impact” with measurable outcomes if available: number of livestreams, frequency of video series, audience growth, or production volume.
- Clarify supervision modestly: “provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate” or “helped onboard and guide…”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this version framed as launching/building the capability, not scaling it.
- “Strengthening workflows” is repeated elsewhere; here, specify that you helped establish early processes rather than led enterprise governance.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows the start of your multimedia/digital trajectory, but it reads generic and underplays impact. Since later NACo roles already cover broad digital leadership, this item should emphasize distinctive “firsts” and concrete outputs.

Suggested edit
- Reframe around unique contribution and tighten scope: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting program development and policy communications.”
- Make the podcast launch the lead achievement: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- Condense the rest into one supporting clause: “Produced digital and multimedia content to translate research and program work into member-facing communications materials.”
- If possible, add volume/outcome metrics: number of projects supported, podcast episodes produced, audiences reached, or types of stakeholders/programs served.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this item focused on research/program support plus the first podcast launch.
- Avoid broad “supporting organizational programs and policy work” language unless you can specify the initiative or result.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but reads as a mixed list of software and capabilities. It also overlaps with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” and several work bullets, so it should be tightened to emphasize tools only or framed more strategically.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: **Creative & Production Tools**
